notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Does Race Affect Access to Government Services?: An Experiment Exploring Street-Level Bureaucrats and Access to Public Housing, by Katherine Levine Einstein and David M. Glick, dated November 7, 2015, Forthcoming American Journal of Political Science. Title, authors, subject and journal match the neutral original reference. DOI is not printed in the inspected text; this is a primary author manuscript, not the final 2016/2017 typeset article. Text contains main results and supporting-information tables through SI8; no PDF was supplied. Input study_o, description and es_type_o are null and locators_o is empty, so no specific outcome, contrast or model identifies the assigned effect. Candidates include response rates (white/black p=.41; white/Hispanic difference 4.8 percentage points, p=.11; black/Hispanic about 8 percentage points, p=.02), a likelihood-ratio test of race indicators (chi-square=4.49, p=.106), response speed, and named greeting (white/Hispanic raw comparison p=.000; adjusted Hispanic logit coefficient -0.82 with p<0.01 in Table 1). These are distinct tests and must not be merged. Table 1 prints model observation counts 978 (response), 551 (response in 24 hours) and 549 (proper name greeting); SI2 additionally prints 991 for its unadjusted responsiveness model. None is assigned to this row because the critical test is unspecified. No N summation or effect-size conversion was performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
